text: To understand the knight, go back to Nib's world: nine towers holding a mountain pass, and a black tide of faceless monsters climbing toward them.
The commander gives Nib one order, and one promise.
A young scout, Kett, begs Nib to come with him. Nib presses a sealed message into his hands instead.
Kett runs, clutching the message, looking back the whole way.
Far away, the sound every soldier on that wall was waiting for.
And Nib holds the gatehouse alone as they pour over the wall.
One scratch in the stone for every day he holds it.
Then he turns and looks down the pass where the army went. The road is empty.
Back in the boss room, the knight raises its sword over them, and Jaeha gives the only order that makes sense.
For the first time, Nib refuses an order. Not against his commander. Not even now.
Jaeha hauls him behind the pillar by the cloak, a hand's width ahead of the blade.
And the amber glow drains out of Nib's eye.
A window: field form has ended. Nib is back in rest form, and a summon in rest form cannot fight. Cooldown: one minute.
Nib won't look up. For the first time, the scout sounds like a soldier left behind.
Jaeha crouches to his level and gives him a rule nobody on the Ninth Wall ever gave him.
Nib finally looks up at him.
The knight turns slowly in the hall, its red face sweeping the pillars like a searchlight.
But Jaeha is reading the floor. He has seen these plates before, in the corridor where his husk shattered. And there are spike holes in the pillars.
Out comes the notebook, and the hall becomes a map.
The plan, from above: the knight's path across the plates, and one small circle past the arch where somebody has to stand.
He has the knight's one habit, and a plan that needs bait.
Yerin grabs his sleeve. She thinks he means to fight it.
Jaeha just grins. Bait is the one job he has always been good at.
The notebook snaps shut. The plan is ready.
Then he strolls out across the open floor toward the arch, hands in his pockets.
Nib watches him go, knuckles tight on his knives.
He stops just past the arch and calls to it as politely as he'd greet a client.
The knight charges straight at him across the plates.
Its iron foot comes down on the big centre plate. Click.
Spikes burst from both pillars and lock its legs.
Then the rusted portcullis slams down on its back, driving it to its knees.
The boss is pinned under the portcullis, and Jaeha never laid a hand on it.
Yerin's jaw drops. An F-rank just did what the whole guild couldn't.
But the gauntlets close on the bars, and the bars start to bend. Twelve seconds of cooldown left.
It rams its helm into the bars, red light flaring in Jaeha's face.
So he gives Yerin the job only she can do: be the brightest thing in the room.
Yerin steps out, and her palms blaze mint-white across the hall.
Something bright and alive. The knight twists toward it and swings blindly at her pillar.
The sword bites the stone a hand's width above her head.
Jaeha bangs on the bars to pull it back toward himself.
Across the hall, Yerin is starting to understand what trap-testing really means.
Jaeha, sweating, gives her a thumbs-up.
Nib watches a small orange figure stand in front of a giant, so the others don't have to. A scout's job.
Then the spikes snap, one after another, and the bars bow. Three seconds.
The knight tears the whole portcullis out of the arch and knocks Jaeha flat.
Flat on his back, Jaeha sees the window he needs. Cooldown zero. Nib can take field form again.
Jaeha calls him back. A cyan circle flashes under Nib, and the amber floods back into his eye.
He looks across the hall at Jaeha. Nobody has ever called him back before.
Jaeha grins up from the dust. A promise kept, for once.
And a window: Nib answered a second call by choice. Seal two of five. His power doubles, from twenty percent to forty.
The seal breaks, and the Ninth Wall's colours flood back into his cloak, with the nine-tower sigil at his throat.
The knight's sword comes down on Jaeha, and Nib catches it on crossed knives. This time, his feet don't slide an inch.
He looks back over his shoulder. Some lines he still won't cross.
For Jaeha, that is more than enough.
Then, deep in the empty helm, the red light flickers and turns a cold, pale white.
The knight stops pushing and leans down until its helm is level with Nib's face.
And out of that hole comes a voice, deep and clear. It knows his name.
Nib's pupil shrinks to a dot.
Jaeha stares up from the floor. Three hundred and twelve raids, and he has never heard a boss speak.
The light steadies, and the voice asks Nib for the one thing he refused.
Whatever the Hush is, it has already taken his commander.
